headline: Timms Review calls for overhaul of PIP disability benefit, with 15 fixes to the current system

terms.meaning: Personal Independence Payment, a benefit for people with long-term illness or disability to help with extra costs.
A service that helps people explain their needs and speak up for themselves.
The Office for Budget Responsibility, the official body that forecasts public spending.

levels.headline: Timms Review calls for overhaul of PIP disability benefit, with 15 fixes to the current system
levels.body:
The Timms Review of Personal Independence Payment (PIP) published its final report on 24 November. It recommends fixing the current system now and moving towards a reformed benefit in the longer term.
For the existing system it makes 15 recommendations. They include fewer unnecessary reviews of awards for people with lifelong or degenerative conditions, a better PIP2 claim form with clearer guidance, and better assessment of conditions that fluctuate. It also proposes an independent advocacy service for claimants who struggle to explain how their condition affects them, random quality checks using recorded assessments, and a recognised professional path for assessors.
For the longer term, cash would stay at the centre of the benefit. Options include tailored help, a voluntary scheme to swap part of the cash for a service, and referrals to services such as social care. People with serious, well-evidenced conditions would be fast-tracked without a full assessment. Support would not be a condition of getting the award.
Any changes must fit within the Office for Budget Responsibility's spending projections.
levels.why: It affects the disabled people who rely on PIP and shapes how much the government spends on the benefit.

The S&P 500 closed down on Tuesday 24 November, the last completed session, falling 0.5% (36.08 points) to 7,201.09 from 7,237.17. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54. The Dow Jones Industrial Average bucked the trend, gaining 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70, helped by Amgen, Nike and Salesforce.

headline: UK inflation rises to 3.6% in October as the Bank of England lifts rates to 4% and warns of 5%

terms.meaning: The rate at which prices rise over time.

levels.headline: UK inflation rises to 3.6% in October as the Bank of England lifts rates to 4% and warns of 5%
levels.body:
UK consumer price inflation rose to 3.6% in the 12 months to October 2026, up from 3.5% in September, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said on 18 November. Prices rose 0.5% on the month. Core inflation, which excludes energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, was 2.8%, and CPIH, which includes housing costs for owner-occupiers, was 3.7%. Goods inflation rose to 3.5%, its highest since September 2023, while food inflation eased to 0.8% from 1.2%.
The figure came in just below the 3.7% economists had expected.
On 5 November the Bank of England raised its main interest rate by a quarter of a point to 4%, its first rise in more than three years. The vote was 8 to 1, with one member wanting a rise to 4.25%. The Bank now expects inflation to reach about 5% by the middle of 2027, linking this to the Middle East conflict and energy prices. Governor Andrew Bailey said that without news that eases the inflation risks, he sees the case for a further rise.

headline: UK unemployment is 4.6% as regular pay growth slows to 3.5%, the ONS says

terms.meaning: The share of people who want a job but do not have one.

levels.headline: UK unemployment is 4.6% as regular pay growth slows to 3.5%, the ONS says
levels.body:
UK unemployment was 4.6% in the three months to September 2026, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS) labour market figures released on 17 November. The ONS said the rate was down 0.3 percentage points on both the quarter and the year.
Pay growth slowed. Average regular earnings, excluding bonuses, rose 3.5% in July to September, down from 3.7% in the previous three-month period. Total earnings including bonuses grew 3.6%. The ONS linked the slowdown in regular pay to weaker public sector pay growth.
The economic inactivity rate, which counts working-age people who are neither working nor looking for work, fell to 20.8%, down 0.1 points on the year.
The figures matter to the Bank of England, which is trying to bring inflation down and raised rates to 4% on 5 November. The next labour market release is due on 15 December.
levels.why: Jobs and pay affect household incomes and influence the Bank of England's interest rate decisions.

levels.headline: COP31 climate talks end without a deal after the EU and others reject a draft that omitted fossil fuels
levels.body:
The COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended on Sunday 22 November without an agreement. The European Union, the UK and other countries rejected a final draft because it did not mention fossil fuels. COP31 President Murat Kurum acknowledged at the closing session that the decisions had not been adopted.
An earlier draft had called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, but a second version released on Thursday removed every mention of them. More than 130 countries had wanted the deal to reaffirm the COP28 commitment to transition away from fossil fuels. A target of about €110 billion a year in adaptation finance by 2035 also dropped out of the final draft.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres said he was deeply disappointed. Ireland's climate minister, speaking for the EU, said the conference had been hijacked by some oil states. More than 90 countries did back a pledge to raise electricity's share of global final energy use from about 23% to 35% by 2035. Ethiopia will host COP32 next year.

Spain votes in a snap general election on Sunday 29 November, and four polls published on 22 November all put Alberto Núñez Feijóo's centre-right People's Party (PP) ahead of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's Socialists (PSOE). The gap ranges from 0.5 percentage points in an Ipsos poll to 6.4 points in one by Hamalgama Métrica.
One poll by GAD3 gave the PP 31.1% and 131 seats, the PSOE 28.4% and 110 seats, and the far-right Vox 18.1% and 63 seats. A party needs 176 of the 350 seats for a majority, so the PP would probably need Vox's support, and the polls put the two together at between 190 and 210 seats.
A separate poll for elDiario.es found that 58% of respondents had a bad or very bad opinion of Sánchez, against 41% with a good or very good one. Sánchez called the early election in October.
levels.why: The result will decide who governs Spain, a major EU economy, and could shift the balance of European politics.

Four polls published on 22 November all put the centre-right People's Party (PP), led by Alberto Núñez Feijóo, in front of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's Socialists. The size of the lead varies from half a point to more than six points.
In one poll, the PP had 131 seats, the Socialists 110 and the far-right party Vox 63. A party needs 176 seats out of 350 to govern with a majority. The PP would probably need Vox's help, and the polls suggest those two parties together could win between 190 and 210 seats.
A separate poll found 58% of people had a bad opinion of Sánchez. He called the election in October.
levels.why: The result will decide who governs Spain, a major EU economy, and could shift the balance of European politics.
